name: Pestilent Scar
summary: In the Eastern Plaguelands, ravenous oozes churn across the floor of Pestilent Scar. The hollow seems older than the Scourge blight that fills it.

sections.title: A Blighted Chasm
sections.body: Pestilent Scar cuts through the eastern reaches of the Eastern Plaguelands, a gloomy rift in corrupted land. Nearby, sudden eruptions of the Plague of Undeath tore open Infectis Scar. Pestilent Scar seems to have formed naturally, perhaps as a deep river canyon or a lake that dried when the Scourge swept across Lordaeron. Barren at first, the trench gradually filled with noxious runoff and foul slime.

sections.title: The Slime Pits
sections.body: Without pure water and under constant unholy decay, the hollow now breeds mutated, acidic slimes and carrion vermin. Crossing its crumbling rim is dangerous. Acrid fumes choke the air above the drop, and unstable soil can send the unwary into the churning muck.

faq.answer: Pestilent Scar is a sunken gorge in the Eastern Plaguelands. Corruption took hold during Lordaeron's fall, leaving foul runoff, diseased soil, and aggressive oozes.

faq.q: How did the Pestilent Scar form?
faq.answer: Unlike fissures torn open by Scourge eruptions, Pestilent Scar seems to have begun as a natural valley, lake, or river canyon. The Plague of Undeath blighted it until it dried and withered.

faq.q: How does it differ from the Infectis Scar?
faq.answer: Infectis Scar was violently ripped open as an unnatural volcanic rupture filled with magical blight. Pestilent Scar seems to be an older natural depression that gradually gathered corruption and runoff after the land died.

faq.q: What creatures live in the Pestilent Scar?
faq.answer: Acidic oozes spawned by the plague and carrion-eating vermin live on the chasm floor, among poisonous pools and rotting organic matter.

angles.text: Along the gorge's edges, concentrated rot can nurture rare plants hardened by blight, such as Arthas' Tears and Plaguebloom, along the cliffs.
As an undead traveler, you may know that Forsaken apothecaries study slimes from deep fissures to isolate unstable forms of the Scourge's foulest toxins.
